newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Tuesday, dealers said.

Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June retail sales figures, which are forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent decline reported in May, they said.

"Rates were steady to a little bit higher in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people were waiting for tonight's release of the retail sales figures, for fresh clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But unless the numbers are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he said.

In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent and Wednesday/Thursday rose 3/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8, but week-fixed was unchanged from Monday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, four-months rose 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months rose 1/16 point to 5-3/4 5-5/8 and twelve-months was unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
